reviews.title: Overcomicated & Buggy
reviews.text:
First of all, I absolutely hate apps that are “free”, let you download, make you enter details and makes you think that its working on a custom tailored plan, only to ask for a paid membership plan before actually using the app. I have used and been with this app for several days, and I can say, its well intentioned, but poorly designed. The plan it designed for me is impractical. It takes a bunch of data points and spew out a mathematically progressing plan that is not practical for real world experience. Ramping up protein intake and workout sessions lengths, etc.
I was glad to know that it does allow for a gradual increase or a scheduled plan, which is what I wanted, to build my own plan. The user interface to build a custom plan is very painful. The options you select change as you go through pages. For instance. I added that I want to do resistance training Monday, Wednesday and Friday. It added a Thursday because the day I was adding this task was a Thursday. The visual map it shows of the coming weeks shows random dates selected in addition to your intended date, despite you having selected the general conditions in the precious page. After closing and saving, the app needs a few hours to a day to refresh the plan. Its not instant. Task failures (or in this case Skip) does not make you reset your streak. So I try their “hard mode”, which gives me all kinda unnecessary warnings, adds pushups and what not, and still does not reset the streak! And shows a lot of the  day 1 and day 2 tasks progress and holds the XP you’ve earned, which defeats the purpose of a reset. Failing a task makes it so hard to reset and reconfigure everything, I’m now afraid to fail because of the work I’ll need to do to reset everything - AKA start a new plan, go through the lame AI onboarding page, looking at their stupid plan, doing breathing work, before actually being able to curate a new plan. After paying 60 bucks for an annual plan, I’m realizing I’m now stuck with this lame UI and have to make it work in some stupid way, which defeats the purpose of this app. I might as well have done this with a pen and paper. I will now literally do everything on a paper and return to this app when I can maintain my streak confidentially so that I don’t have to deal with the UI bugs and simple check some boxes on a daily basis. Bravo App!

There should’ve been a trial period before paying the hefty fee for a glamorized (and non functional) to-do list.

reviews.title: Unsure about this app
reviews.text: Loved this app to start, for 48 days. Had subscription and all. Seemed promising. Loved the aspect of looking what loot my character had coming back from a battle. Then the bug happened which lost my streaks. Had that fixed  but more and more bugs keep happening and updates say they fixed them but they haven’t. I JUST updated the newest one and bug keeps happening. I keep editing a task that was relentless with a specific way it wanted to be done and it kept reverting back to the way I didn’t like it to be. So at that point I decided to just get rid of the task from my plan. And that worked for a little while. Now the tasks will not go away no matter how i delete it. then I could no longer see images of the loot my character came back with and it just ruined it for me the longer it went on. I thought the newest update would fix that with other bugs but no matter how many times I log out and restart the app it’s still happening with the task and now I feel the whole interface is just complicated to get to certain things like resetting timer for blocked screen time and meditation. Now I can no longer find a way to look at my loot if it’s still even part of the app. If it’s not I’m just giving up on it. That was the part that drew me to this app for me to stay. 3 stars was me being generous cause I liked how it was before the relentless bugs. Habit legends has no subscriptions, keeps you pulled in with a story line and MUCH MUCH more flexible with editing tasks.

reviews.title: Yeah, You Have to Pay. Yeah, it’s Worth it.
reviews.text:
I (24M) got this app last year after being targeted hard with ads for the app. Needless to say, I’ve REALLY enjoyed it, and the developers are continuously improving the experience.

I’ve used other habit trackers before to no avail, but something about this one just clicks. If I had to describe why, it’s that the app “feels” like it’s on the journey with you. The UI is clean, and I love the art associated with the achievements, the tasks, and the motivation cards.

The task progression is pretty solid too. Where last year mandatory tasks like “wakeup early” were difficult to deal with if you’re on a swing shift like I am, this year it’s been customized to where you can simply achieve a minimum number of hours of rest. Super helpful update.

In future updates, I’d love to see a more “knowledge gaining” or “addiction breaking” or “workout focused” program development. There’s so many extra tasks in the portfolio that don’t get added to the docket unless I manually add them. And while I absolutely can do that, somehow it just takes the magic away, and in my brain makes it more of an “optional” task. If the app automatically built it into day 1 of a more focused program, my brain would perceive it as a much more important and critical task. Not just “an extra thing to do.”

Overall, I love Life Reset. I love watching my “levels” go up, and it’s a reminder that you need to level your self up daily just like you would for a character in a video game. Thank you developers!!!
